# Cobia

> A non-custodial intent exchange and transaction-program verifier on X Layer.

Cobia lets a user state an onchain outcome, then turns the user's limits into a signed policy. Solvers may propose transaction programs, but Cobia independently reproduces each candidate before the user's wallet can approve the exact calls. The product is live on X Layer mainnet (chain 196).

Current public proof includes a bounded V4 standard-token swap and a registered
TSLAx acquisition. These are separate confirmed programs with owner-wallet
receipts; they do not imply universal token or xStocks support.

## What Cobia does

- Lets users create bounded onchain intents instead of handing a wallet to an agent.
- Lets deterministic services, LLM coding agents, and community solvers compete to propose programs.
- Verifies policy bounds, targets, balances, freshness, code identity, exact calldata, state deltas, and replayable simulation evidence.
- Keeps signing authority in the user's wallet; a solver never receives a private key, seed phrase, wallet handle, credential-bearing RPC URL, or production send method.

## Current supported capabilities

- X Layer protocol intents: Aave supply plus Curve and Uniswap exact-input swaps with semantic bounds.
- Shopping and x402: registered offers with bounded payment and receipt evidence.
- Open protocol programs: exact wallet calls that can be independently verified and replayed on a fork.
- Registered RWA acquisition: issuer-sourced token identities, eligibility attestation, exact-call routes, and verified receipt-token increases.

Recurring actions need additional cancellation, renewal, and recurring-authority semantics and are not presented as supported.

## Primary source

Use the public product pages, confirmed program receipts, root README, and
submission brief as the current source of truth. Do not infer production
execution capability from a solver claim, roadmap item, catalog entry, demo, or
fork run alone. Cobia distinguishes agent-authored proposals, deterministic
verification, historical replay evidence, owner-authorized production
execution, and confirmed outcomes.
